title: TOWNS OF REFUGE AMONG THE PRIESTS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Israelites allotted to the Levites these towns and their pasturelands, as the Lord had commanded through Moses. From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they allotted the following towns by name (these towns were assigned to the descendants of Aaron who were of the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot fell to them): They gave them Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), with its surrounding pastureland, in the hill country of Judah. (Arba was the forefather of Anak.) — Josh 21:8-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Among the towns given to Aaron's descendants was Hebron — the same Hebron that was also a city of refuge. This is striking. The priests, who represented God's mercy to the people, lived in the very place where a person who had accidentally killed someone could flee for safety.

Picture it: a frightened person runs to Hebron, pursued and afraid, and the first people he meets are the priests of God. Mercy and worship lived side by side. The place of safety was also the place where God was served.

This points us to Christ so clearly. We too are fugitives who need refuge — not from an avenger of blood, but from the judgment our sin deserves. And in Jesus we find a refuge who is also our Priest. He does not merely shelter us; He is the one who makes peace with God on our behalf (Heb 6:18-20). We run to Him, and we find both safety and the very presence of God.

Notice too the small honest detail: Hebron was once the home of Anak, whose descendants had terrified Israel. The place that once meant fear now means refuge. God turns places of dread into places of grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you run when you are afraid or guilty?
2. How does it comfort you that your refuge, Jesus, is also your Priest?
3. Has God turned a place of fear in your life into a place of grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are my refuge and my Priest. Thank You that in You I find both safety and the presence of God. I run to You today. Amen.
